subject: Separation 'Saga' — topology walkthrough for upcoming audit
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@helio-sec.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: security-audits@greenline.com
Date: 2027-06-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: network/topology narrative + evidence for SIG/CAIQ prep

Hi Irene,

Hope you're well — I'm on the incoming SIG/CAIQ review for Greenline's vendor stack. The reviewers want a concise narrative that ties your deployment types (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) to concrete network isolation controls and fallback behaviour during capacity issues.

Specifically we need:
- A short (1–2 page) narrative that explains how tenant fencing is enforced across Dedicated and Private deployments.
- An annotated topology diagram showing control-plane vs data-plane demarcation and egress breakpoints.
- A short table of fallback/rollover rules: which model variants or regions are used if capacity is constrained.

Deadline is COB next Wednesday (2027-06-16). Can you point me to the latest artifacts or share a short narrative and topology? If you prefer, we can accept a PDF plus an exported CSV of the active fencing rules.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Gomez
Principal Security Reviewer, HelioSec

To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@helio-sec.com>

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We're on it.

Plan:
- Kimberly will produce the 1–2 page narrative and the annotated topology PDF.

- Ben will confirm the rollout/fallback table and provide the short bullet list of behavior.

We should be able to deliver a consolidated packet by EOD 2027-06-15 to give you a buffer before your deadline.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@helio-sec.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: network/topology narrative + evidence for SIG/CAIQ prep

Alex / team — attaching the packet. Summary below, and I pasted the high level diagram legend at the end of this message.

Attachments: redwood_sepsaga_topology_v1.pdf (annotated topology, 2 pages), fencing-rule-list.csv (active rules snapshot)

High-level narrative (short):
Redwood enforces tenant separation across Dedicated and Private deployments using a layered approach:

1) Logical tenancy + network constructs
- Each tenant in Dedicated receives a dedicated set of GPU hosts within a reserved pool and a tenant-anchored VPC segment. Private deployments are customer-managed VPCs where Redwood components run within the customer's subnet allocation.

2) Control-plane / Data-plane demarcation
- Control-plane (management APIs, autoscaler, model catalog) is logically separated and runs in an isolated control VPC with restricted ingress. Evidence: topology page 1, annotated red boxes.
- Data-plane (inference runtime, KV cache) resides in tenant-attached compute zones. KV caches are per-tenant by default for Dedicated; for Private, default is tenant-local unless customer elects shared caching and signs an explicit config.

3) Network enforcement and egress controls
- Microsegmentation (security groups + eBPF rules) enforces one-way flows: tenant compute -> model artifacts storage (read) and to Redwood-managed observability collectors (write-only).
- Egress is restricted at the subnet/NAT layer; documented breakpoints are on page 2.

4) Fallback / rollout behaviour (short table):
- If Dedicated pool capacity in a region is saturated, traffic is routed by policy to: 1) idle Dedicated burst capacity in adjacent AZ (same region) 2) Compatible hosted model variant (lower-cost instance) in a pre-authorized region (if customer allows cross-region fallback).
- For Private deployments, fallbacks are limited — we provide a failover advisory and optional temporary Hosted bridging (requires customer opt-in).

Legend excerpt (diagram):
- Solid blue border: tenant-only compute subnets (no cross-tenant routing)
- Dashed purple border: shared infra (observability, logging collectors)
- Red hatch: control-plane endpoints (management APIs) — restricted CIDR and bastion-only ingress
- Green arrows: approved egress breakpoints (NAT + outbound filter)

Notes:
- The attached CSV is a snapshot of active firewall/security-group rules that implement the microsegmentation references. It includes rule id, source cidr, dest cidr, protocol, and justification.
- We redacted internal hostnames that are not relevant to the audit; if Helio needs host-level artifacts we can provide scoped captures under an NDA.

Will send an updated PDF if you need an additional 'zoom' on the KV-cache boundaries.

Best,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@helio-sec.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, security-audits@greenline.com
Date: 2027-06-15T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: network/topology narrative + evidence for SIG/CAIQ prep

Kimberly — perfect, this is exactly what we needed. The narrative ties the controls to architecture cleanly and the diagram legend is helpful.

A couple quick follow-ups before we close the ticket:
- Can you confirm the default KV-cache scope for Dedicated is per-tenant (you mentioned that) and indicate how it's enforced (config + runtime flag) in one sentence?
- In the fencing CSV, could you add a column 'risk-owner' for each rule (ops, infra, security) so auditors can see ownership?

If you can send brief one-line updates to those two items, we'll attach your packet to the SIG intake and close. Thanks again.

— Alex
